At what age does intussusception occur?
From 3 months to 3 years, with a peak at 5–10 months.
What causes intussusception under 2 years of age?
Swollen Peyer patches after a viral infection; there is no lead point.
What lead points cause intussusception in older children?
Meckel diverticulum, a polyp, lymphoma and Henoch–Schönlein purpura.
What is the pain pattern of intussusception?
Colicky attacks of screaming with the legs drawn up; the child is pale and lethargic between attacks.
What is the stool sign of intussusception, and is it early or late?
A redcurrant jelly stool; it is a late sign.
What is the abdominal sign of intussusception?
A sausage-shaped mass in the right upper abdomen, with an empty right iliac fossa.
What is the best test for intussusception?
Ultrasound, which shows the target (doughnut) sign.
What is the first-line treatment of intussusception?
Reduction by air or saline enema under imaging.

Is abdominal distension an early sign of intussusception?
No. It is a late sign.

What is the pain pattern of appendicitis?
Pain around the umbilicus that moves to the right iliac fossa.
Why is appendicitis often perforated in children under 5?
The signs are vague, so diagnosis is delayed, and the omentum is thin.
What is the first imaging for suspected appendicitis?
Ultrasound: an appendix wider than 6 mm that does not compress.
What are the medical causes of acute abdominal pain?
Lower-lobe pneumonia, diabetic ketoacidosis, urinary tract infection, sickle cell crisis, Henoch–Schönlein purpura and mesenteric adenitis.
What must never be forgotten when examining a boy with abdominal pain?
The scrotum (testicular torsion) and the hernial orifices.
How is recurrent abdominal pain defined?
Four or more episodes in 2 months; 90% are functional.
Which features support functional abdominal pain?
Pain around the umbilicus, normal growth and no pain at night.
What are the red flags in recurrent abdominal pain?
Pain away from the umbilicus, waking at night, weight loss, blood in the stool and fever.
How is functional abdominal pain managed?
By explanation and reassurance, keeping the child at school, and reducing stress.

What is the "rule of 2" for Meckel diverticulum?
It occurs in 2% of people, 2 feet from the ileocaecal valve, is 2 inches long, contains 2 types of ectopic tissue and usually presents under 2 years.
What is the classic presentation of Meckel diverticulum?
Painless massive rectal bleeding in a toddler.
Why does a Meckel diverticulum bleed?
Ectopic gastric mucosa makes acid that ulcerates the ileum.
